explanation: Very sparse, weak feature (max 0.16). About 80% of activation mass is in the original phase on the token right after two consecutive h inputs, almost always at t=2 (sequence starts h h X) or t=3 (? h h X). The following token matters: t, 2, b, j, v, r and k fire most reliably; d, p, u fire weakly and a, w often not at all. The same h h X pattern later in the sequence (t>=4) rarely fires. The remaining ~20% of mass is a diffuse copy-phase piece, mostly the input t at early copy steps (e.g. t g ... <DEL> [t] g), often where g or h follows in the original. No predicate captured it precisely, so it is left out. Precision is limited because many early h h X steps with the listed tokens still do not fire. It never fires at t=0-1 or on the delimiter step.
